subject.title: [Bug]: Memory detection skips macOS (darwin) — os.freemem() / os.totalmem() never reported to agent on non-Linux platforms

question: Should macOS startup optimization hints target all Apple Silicon Macs like Linux ARM, or only low-memory Darwin hosts?
rationale: The code change is small, but the current helper copy and prior PRs expose a user-facing policy choice about when macOS users should see low-power host guidance.

options.title: Low-memory Darwin only
options.body: Add Darwin support for constrained Macs, keep Linux ARM behavior unchanged, update note copy to be platform-neutral, and cover Darwin low/high-memory tests.

options.title: Match Linux ARM behavior
options.body: Treat all Darwin ARM hosts as startup-tuning targets and update wording/tests so broad Apple Silicon guidance is intentional.

options.title: Keep Linux-only
options.body: Close or defer the request if maintainers want this startup optimization guidance to remain Linux-specific for now.

recommendation.title: Low-memory Darwin only
recommendation.body: Add Darwin support for constrained Macs, keep Linux ARM behavior unchanged, update note copy to be platform-neutral, and cover Darwin low/high-memory tests.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc introduced the helper and original Linux-only startup optimization policy in the merged feature history.
